title: Gap-Stitcher KV allocator and fragmentation inspector for live KV cache compaction
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: The model KV cache exhibits external fragmentation under real-world request mixes (variable sequence lengths, intermittent long generations, tenant heterogeneity). Fragmentation reduces usable contiguous memory and forces lower effective KV capacity or expensive full-shard evacuations. This ticket specifies a bounded, low-latency remediation strategy: a new allocator variant ('Gap-Stitcher') plus a light-weight Fragmentation Inspector (FI) that drives constrained background coalescing and micro-migrations to reduce fragmentation while keeping decode tail latencies within SLOs.
proposed_solution: Overview: Implement Gap-Stitcher allocator that tracks free runs as small compressed 'gaps' and performs three remediation primitives: (A) stitch: coalesce adjacent gaps in-place when contiguous, (B) micro-migrate: move small sets of cold KV entries into a compact target span using an indirection table for migrated slots, (C) evacuate-and-reclaim: scheduled larger reclaims during low-traffic windows. Add a Fragmentation Inspector agent that samples allocation maps, computes per-GPU fragmentation heat, and enforces copy and latency budgets before triggering remediation. Implementation components: runtime/kv/allocator/gap_stitcher.cc (C++), runtime/kv/inspector (sampling + policy engine), runtime/config flags for per-tenant budgets. Use cudaMemcpyAsync with a dedicated low-priority stream for migrations; prefer P2P copy when available. Use pinned staging buffers for device-host-device copies when required. Keep fast-path lookup simple: direct slot->pointer mapping; only migrated slots consult small indirection table.
tradeoffs_and_design_considerations:
- Migration cost vs fragmentation: We prefer frequent small micro-migrations to rare large evacuations to limit max pause and memory pressure spikes.
- Indirection overhead: Only enabled for migrated slots to avoid lookup-time penalties for hot, resident entries.
- GPU copy strategy: Async copies reduce stalls but consume DMA/PCIe bandwidth; a token-bucket controls copy rate.
- Metadata size: Gap map must stay compact; we compress runs and periodically trim metadata.
- Scheduling: Inspector triggers must avoid busy decode windows; add SLO-aware suppression and backoff.
acceptance_criteria: free_contiguous_ratio improves by >=20% on targeted synthetic churn benchmark
P95/P99 decode latency regression <5% compared to baseline under production-like traffic
Allocator metadata overhead <3% of KV payload bytes on typical models
Feature toggles available per-tenant and per-model; default to disabled for customers on strict SLAs
Dashboards and alerts for compaction_pressure and migration_rate exist and are validated
rollout_plan: Implement feature branch and unit/integration tests (allocator invariants + migration correctness)
Run microbenchmarks on staging GPUs: A100 (production), T4 (edge) with controlled sequences and churn traces
Canary on 5% of traffic for non-critical tenants with low compaction_budget; collect 72h telemetry
If stable, ramp to 25% then 50% with tuned budgets; full rollout gated on telemetry and perf review
Post-rollout: scheduled weekly low-traffic evacuation window for final compaction pass
telemetry_queries: fragmentation_heat: distribution of free-run lengths per-GPU and percentiles
migration_rate: micro-migrations/sec broken down by mode (stitch,micro,evacuate)
compaction_pressure: inspector triggers/minute and triggers that were suppressed due to SLOs
allocator_overhead_bytes: metadata vs payload ratio sampled per-model
experiment_plan: Synthetic replay: replay 24h of production traces with injected long generations to stress fragmentation
A/B: serve identical traffic with current allocator vs gap-stitcher behind feature flag; compare P95/P99 and memory density
Soak: 7-day soak on staging with periodic bursts to observe slow drift and eviction churn
implementation_notes: Locking: per-shard fine-grained locks; lookup path uses optimistic reads with CAS fallback
Copy budgeting: per-GPU token bucket charged by bytes copied; policy engine decrements tokens when scheduling migrations
Config knobs: stitch_threshold_bytes, micro_migrate_batch_size, allow_indirection (true/false), inspector_sampling_rate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Background copies contend with decode -> mitigation: low-priority CUDA stream + strict token-bucket + SLO suppression
Risk: Metadata growth leads to memory bloat -> mitigation: periodic metadata compaction + max metadata size enforcement
Risk: Cross-GPU migrations create PCIe pressure -> mitigation: prefer local placement and P2P; schedule cross-GPU only during low load windows
